## Body

Open for receiver-edge retry or lapse recovery reviews.

Producer-only renewal tests prove eventual persistence, not safe policy input
between heartbeats. Use a real-store cross-service witness: lapse not yet decided,
mechanical renewal succeeds, renewed audit append fails, then recovery reconciles
before another heartbeat. At #320 head 5c219c0, receiver_reason is None but a
restart is queued because outstanding only sees the stale spine lapse.

Audit-pending and mechanically-lapsed cannot share deduplication identity blindly.
A receiver renewed once, lost its renewal audit, then genuinely expired before
another heartbeat; #320's reinserted native_lapsed mark suppressed the second
lapse edge. If the earlier lapse was decided, recovery sees no outstanding loss.
The stronger probe restored a forty-minute-old decision into an empty ledger:
one edge and zero restart controls; removing only the added reinsert restored
two edges and one restart. Check a later real loss, not just another audit retry.

Positive controls matter: F260 returned the old held body once and a new live
send stayed queued, not parked. A gap during throttle sleep was caught on durable
reconcile; daemon shutdown aborts and joins the follower, so its pending sleep
does not need a separate inner stop select. Held decisions survive empty-ledger
restart, newer edges remain eligible, and held does not refresh the acting window.

Mutation controls killed no-wait, no-reinsert, ignored-held and missing-held-write
variants; each original upstream test passed. The isolated probe used real time
with a one-second test-only lease. Paused Tokio expired real SQLite pool deadlines
before behavior; do not mistake those fixture failures for product evidence.

Magic wand: keep renewal-failure -> policy-consumer -> next-lifetime orderings as
daemon regression tests, rather than stopping at the producer's next heartbeat.
